ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-Step Token Generator Matched to a Frozen Teacher by Distribution Matching
PROPOSAL: Train a feed-forward generator that maps a Gaussian latent to a full sequence of 256 codebook tokens. Keep a class-conditional autoregressive teacher frozen, and fit a second autoregressive model on the generator's own samples. Update the generator with the gap between the teacher's and the auxiliary model's conditional probabilities, evaluated on generator outputs, so that the output distribution moves toward the teacher without any fixed noise-to-data pairing. Evaluate on ImageNet generation at 256 by 256 pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare Frechet inception distance with the teacher sampled token by token, with a published one-step distillation that relies on a predefined mapping, and with a set-prediction sampler using a similar number of steps. Repeat with three seeds and track training time needed to reach the same score.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: The generator should close most of the gap to the teacher and train faster than the mapping-based distillation. The idea fails if the auxiliary model lags behind the generator and the score plateaus far above the teacher.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training of a Single-Pass Token Sequence Generator
PROPOSAL: Train a generator that produces all codebook tokens of an image from one latent draw, together with a discriminator that reads whole token sequences and separates generator outputs from sequences sampled by a frozen autoregressive teacher. Add a term that rewards the teacher's conditional probability of each generated token given the tokens before it, so the discriminator does not have to carry the whole signal. Use class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token, against the same generator trained with the discriminator alone, and against the same generator trained with the teacher term alone. Repeat with three seeds and track training stability across runs.
COST: 128
PREDICTION: Combining both terms should give a better score than either alone and stay close to the teacher. The idea fails if the discriminator dominates and training oscillates, or if the teacher term alone already reaches the same score.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Straight-Through Relaxation for Distilling Autoregressive Image Models
PROPOSAL: Build a one-step generator whose final layer outputs a categorical distribution per position, then draw relaxed one-hot samples with a temperature that decays during training. Feed the relaxed tokens into the frozen teacher and minimise the reverse divergence between the generator's sequence distribution and the teacher's conditional probabilities. Anneal the temperature on a fixed schedule and switch to hard samples near the end. Train on class-conditional ImageNet tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare against hard sampling with a straight-through gradient estimator, against the teacher sampled token by token, and against a published one-step distillation. Repeat with three seeds and compare the stability of gradients across temperatures.
COST: 800
PREDICTION: Relaxed sampling should give smoother training and a lower score than hard sampling alone. The idea fails if relaxation bias leaves the final hard-sample quality worse than the straight-through estimator.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Small-Scale Pilot of One-Step Distillation on Low-Resolution Tokens
PROPOSAL: Train a small autoregressive teacher on 32 by 32 images from CIFAR-10 encoded with a 512-entry codebook, then distil a single-pass generator from it using distribution matching. Because the sequences are short, the pilot lets us inspect token correlations directly and check, before any large run, that the generator keeps the joint structure that set prediction loses.
CONTROLS: Compare against set prediction with the same number of steps, against the teacher sampled token by token, and against a generator that predicts each token independently. Repeat with five seeds.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: The generator should keep pairwise token correlations close to the teacher, unlike the independent variant. The pilot fails if correlations collapse or if the score trails the set-prediction sampler.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Latent Prior Design for One-Step Autoregressive Image Generators
PROPOSAL: Study how the prior over the input latent affects a single-pass generator distilled from a frozen teacher. Compare a Gaussian latent of 64, 256 and 1024 dimensions, a per-position latent with one vector for each token, and a class-conditioned latent. Keep the generator body and the matching objective fixed, and measure image quality, diversity and training speed on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels.
CONTROLS: Compare each prior against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeat with three seeds, and check whether diversity changes with latent dimension.
COST: 1800
PREDICTION: A per-position latent should improve diversity over a single global vector while quality stays flat. The study fails to support this if all priors reach nearly the same score and diversity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Initialising the One-Step Generator from Teacher Weights
PROPOSAL: Copy the weights of the frozen teacher into a bidirectional generator, replace the causal attention mask with full attention, and fine-tune with a distribution-matching objective. This start gives the generator the teacher's token embeddings and most of its layers, so training begins close to a useful solution. Measure training speed and final quality on class-conditional ImageNet against a generator that starts from random weights.
CONTROLS: Compare against random initialisation, against the teacher sampled token by token, and against a published one-step distillation that trains its student from scratch. Repeat with three seeds and chart score against training steps.
COST: 220
PREDICTION: Copying teacher weights should reach a given score in far fewer steps than random initialisation. The idea fails if the full attention mask destroys the pretrained features and the benefit disappears.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scaling One-Step Distillation to a Billion-Parameter Autoregressive Teacher
PROPOSAL: Distil a single-pass generator from a class-conditional autoregressive teacher with about one billion parameters, using the same distribution-matching recipe as in smaller runs. Train generators of three widths and measure whether quality scales with generator width while the teacher stays fixed. Evaluate on ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance, Inception score and precision-recall.
CONTROLS: Compare each generator width against the teacher sampled token by token, against a published one-step distillation, and against a smaller teacher distilled the same way. Repeat the best configuration with three seeds.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Quality should improve with generator width and approach the teacher. The study fails if the gap to the teacher stays constant across widths or grows with teacher size.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Progressive Step Reduction Toward a Single Forward Pass
PROPOSAL: Train a generator in stages that cut the number of forward passes from eight to four, two and finally one, initialising each stage from the one before. Each stage matches the output distribution of the frozen teacher with the same objective, and the last stage removes all iteration. Evaluate on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels after every stage to see where quality starts to fall.
CONTROLS: Compare against a generator trained directly at one pass, against the teacher sampled token by token, and against set prediction at each matching step count. Repeat with three seeds.
COST: 60
PREDICTION: Quality should degrade gently across stages, ending better than the directly trained one-pass generator. The idea fails if the final stage scores no better than direct training.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Mode Coverage of One-Step Generators Across Classes
PROPOSAL: Take a trained one-step generator and its teacher, draw 50 images per class for all 1000 classes, and compare class-wise precision, recall and diversity. Look for classes where the generator drops modes the teacher keeps, and relate the loss to class frequency and to image complexity. The aim is to see whether distribution matching preserves rare modes better than distillation through a fixed mapping.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher, against a published one-step distillation, and against a generator trained with a mode-seeking objective. Repeat sampling with five seeds and use bootstrap intervals over classes.
COST: 260
PREDICTION: Distribution matching should keep more rare modes than the mapping-based model, with losses concentrated in complex classes. The analysis fails if mode loss looks the same for all methods.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Toy Correlation Test for One-Step Token Generators
PROPOSAL: Construct synthetic token sequences with strong dependencies, such as pairs that must be equal or sequences that copy an earlier position, and train a small teacher on them. Distil a single-pass generator and measure whether the joint distribution of the generated tokens matches the teacher's, using exact probabilities that can be enumerated for short sequences.
CONTROLS: Compare against independent per-position prediction, against set prediction with matched steps, and against the teacher sampled token by token. Repeat with ten seeds, since each run is cheap.
COST: 16
PREDICTION: The generator should reproduce the dependencies while independent prediction spreads mass over invalid combinations. The test fails if the generator also spreads mass over combinations the teacher never produces.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Single-Pass Token Sampler Distilled from a Frozen Autoregressive Teacher
PROPOSAL: Train a generator that turns a Gaussian latent into all 256 codebook tokens of a class-conditional image in one forward pass, keeping the teacher frozen. The generator learns from the teacher's next-token probabilities evaluated on its own outputs, with an auxiliary autoregressive model fitted to those outputs to estimate the gap between the two distributions. Evaluate on ImageNet generation at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance, Inception score and precision-recall.
CONTROLS: Compare Frechet inception distance with the teacher sampled token by token on the same classes. Compare against a published one-step distillation built on a predefined noise-to-data mapping. Compare against a set-prediction sampler using a matched number of steps. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The generator should land close to the teacher's score and train faster than the mapping-based distillation. The claim fails if its score stays far above the teacher or if training diverges without the auxiliary model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: One-Pass Image Token Generator Guided by an Autoregressive Prior
PROPOSAL: Fit a network that maps a Gaussian latent to every one of 256 codebook tokens for a class label at a single evaluation, with the teacher kept frozen. Its training signal is the teacher's conditional next-token probabilities on the network's own samples, plus an auxiliary autoregressive model trained on those samples to measure how far apart the distributions are. Judge it on ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance, Inception score and precision-recall.
CONTROLS: Compare Frechet inception distance with a smaller teacher sampled token by token on the same classes. Compare against a published one-step distillation built on a diffusion model. Compare against a speculative-decoding sampler using a matched number of steps. Repeat training with three seeds.
COST: 240
PREDICTION: The generator should land close to the smaller teacher's score and train faster than the diffusion distillation. The claim fails if its score stays far above that score or if training diverges without the auxiliary model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Matching Weight and Auxiliary Update Rate in One-Step Distillation
PROPOSAL: Build the generator as a bidirectional transformer that receives a latent vector plus a class embedding and emits logits for all 256 positions at once. The training loss combines a matching term computed from the frozen teacher's conditional probabilities with a term from an auxiliary autoregressive model fitted to generator samples. Evaluate class-conditional ImageNet samples at 256 by 256 pixels using Frechet inception distance and Inception score.
CONTROLS: Vary the weight on the matching term among low, medium and high values with the auxiliary update rate held fixed. Vary the number of auxiliary-model updates per generator update. Compare against the teacher sampled token by token. Repeat each run across seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Quality should be best at a medium weight and improve as auxiliary updates become more frequent, then flatten. Failure shows up as a score that does not respond to either factor, or as instability at high weight.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Convolutional Upsampling Generator Distilled from a Token-Level Teacher
PROPOSAL: Use a convolutional upsampling network that starts from a latent vector and a class embedding and emits logits for the 256 positions of the token grid together. Training relies on a loss that mixes teacher conditional probabilities on generator samples with a term from an auxiliary autoregressive model fitted to those samples. Evaluate class-conditional ImageNet samples at 256 by 256 pixels using Frechet inception distance and Inception score.
CONTROLS: Vary the strength of horizontal-flip augmentation among low, medium and high values with the auxiliary update rate held fixed. Vary the number of decoder channels in the tokenizer. Compare against the teacher sampled token by token. Repeat each run across seeds.
COST: 600
PREDICTION: Quality should be best at a medium augmentation strength and improve as decoder channels grow, then flatten. Failure shows up as a score that does not respond to either factor, or as instability at high strength.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Single-Step Sampling on Long Token Sequences
PROPOSAL: Distil a generator that emits an entire image's tokens in one forward pass from a frozen class-conditional teacher, using a distribution-matching loss. Use ImageNet tokenised into 256 positions per image, so that dependencies between neighbouring tokens are strong and long-range. Score samples with Frechet inception distance and precision-recall against held-out images.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on sequences of 256 tokens at one step, where token correlations matter. Compare against the teacher sampled token by token. Compare against a set-prediction sampler at the same step count. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: A set-prediction sampler should degrade clearly at one step on long sequences while the distilled generator stays near the teacher. The claim fails if the generator degrades as much as the set-prediction sampler.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Short-Sequence Tokens for Distribution-Matching Distillation
PROPOSAL: Train a generator that emits a short image token sequence in a few forward passes from a frozen class-conditional teacher, using a distribution-matching loss. Use ImageNet tokenised at coarse granularity into 16 positions per image, so that each token covers a wide area and dependencies between neighbouring tokens are weak. Score samples with Frechet inception distance and precision-recall against held-out images.
CONTROLS: Evaluate on sequences of 16 tokens at sixteen steps, where token correlations are weak. Compare against the teacher sampled token by token. Compare against a set-prediction sampler at the same step count. Repeat across seeds.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: A set-prediction sampler should degrade little at sixteen steps on short sequences while the distilled generator stays near the teacher. The claim fails if the generator degrades as much as the set-prediction sampler.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distribution-Level Measurements for a Distilled One-Step Generator
PROPOSAL: Train a latent-to-sequence generator for class-conditional ImageNet tokens, using the frozen teacher's conditional probabilities on generated sequences as the training signal. Alongside image samples, store the generated token sequences so the teacher can score them directly. The generator is a transformer with full attention over 256 positions, trained for a fixed number of iterations on tokens from a standard image tokenizer.
CONTROLS: Measure Frechet inception distance against held-out ImageNet images. Measure the teacher's average log-likelihood of generated token sequences against teacher samples. Measure precision and recall of generated images. Compare each against the teacher sampled token by token, repeating with seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Frechet inception distance and the teacher's log-likelihood should both land near the teacher's own values. The result fails if the generated sequences score poorly under the teacher even when image scores look fine.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Tokenizer-Side Diagnostics for One-Step Sequence Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a latent-to-sequence network for class-conditional ImageNet tokens with the frozen teacher's conditional probabilities on its samples as the objective. Generated token sequences are logged next to the decoded images for later inspection. The network is a transformer with full attention over 256 positions and runs for a fixed number of iterations on codes from a standard image tokenizer.
CONTROLS: Measure tokenizer reconstruction error on held-out ImageNet images. Measure the average codebook usage of generated token sequences against teacher samples. Measure decoder reconstruction error of generated images. Compare each against the teacher sampled token by token, repeating with seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Reconstruction error and codebook usage should both stay near the teacher's own values. The result fails if the generated sequences drift far in usage even when reconstructions look fine.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Teacher Comparison at Identical Sampling Settings for One-Step Students
PROPOSAL: Train a one-pass generator from a frozen class-conditional teacher with a distribution-matching loss and an auxiliary autoregressive model fitted to generator samples. Because sampling temperature and guidance change the teacher's output distribution, fix both for the training targets and evaluation, and read results at 256 by 256 pixels on ImageNet with Frechet inception distance.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher at the same temperature and guidance scale. Compare against a published one-step distillation trained for the same number of iterations. Compare against a variant whose auxiliary model is frozen after its first fit. Repeat with seeds.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: The generator should come close to the teacher at the shared settings, and the frozen-auxiliary variant should lag behind. The idea fails if the variant with the frozen auxiliary model scores as well as the full method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Shared Targets for a Distilled Single-Evaluation Image Token Generator
PROPOSAL: Fit a single-evaluation generator against a frozen class-conditional teacher, using a distribution-matching objective together with an auxiliary autoregressive model trained on generator samples. Because teacher outputs shift with temperature and guidance, choose one pair of values for training and scoring, and read ImageNet results at 256 by 256 pixels using Frechet inception distance.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher at a higher temperature and a stronger guidance scale. Compare against a published one-step distillation trained for a fraction of the iterations. Compare against a variant whose auxiliary model is trained on teacher samples. Repeat with seeds.
COST: 72
PREDICTION: The generator should come close to the teacher at those other settings, and the teacher-sample variant should lag behind. The idea fails if the variant with the teacher-sample model scores as well as the full method.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distribution Matching for a Frozen Teacher with an Auxiliary Sequence Model
PROPOSAL: Train a latent-to-sequence generator by minimizing the gap between teacher and generator distributions. The frozen class-conditional teacher supplies next-token probabilities on generator samples, while an auxiliary autoregressive model trained on those samples supplies the generator's own conditionals. Evaluate on ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance, comparing one-step quality with the teacher.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeating with seeds.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: The generator should reach one-step scores much closer to the teacher than the mapping-based distillation. The direction fails if the auxiliary model cannot track the generator and scores stay far from the teacher.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Trained Draft Models with Tree Verification for Faster Decoding
PROPOSAL: Train a small draft network that proposes several tokens per round and let the frozen teacher verify branches of a candidate tree in parallel. Measure the average number of tokens accepted per teacher evaluation and the end-to-end speed on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels, while checking that samples keep the teacher's Frechet inception distance.
CONTROLS: Compare against standard token-by-token decoding and against a published draft-and-verify method, repeating with seeds.
COST: 360
PREDICTION: Accepted tokens per round should rise with a larger draft network, giving a several-fold reduction in teacher evaluations. The direction fails if acceptance stays low on detailed images.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Discriminator over Whole Token Sequences
PROPOSAL: Train a latent-to-sequence generator against a discriminator that reads complete token sequences, using sequences drawn from the frozen teacher as positives and generator outputs as negatives. Add a teacher-probability term to steady training. Evaluate on ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance, comparing one-step quality with the teacher.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeating with seeds.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: The generator should reach one-step scores near the teacher, with the probability term preventing collapse. The direction fails if the discriminator dominates and scores oscillate.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Larger Codebooks for Sharper Tokenizer Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Train image tokenizers with enlarged codebooks and a stronger decoder, then measure reconstruction fidelity on held-out ImageNet images at 256 by 256 pixels with Frechet inception distance and pixel error. Keep the downstream autoregressive model fixed in size and check that code usage stays balanced across entries as the codebook grows.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard codebook and against a published tokenizer with factorized codes, repeating with seeds.
COST: 900
PREDICTION: Reconstruction fidelity should improve steadily as the codebook grows, with usage staying balanced. The direction fails if added entries stay unused or if gains flatten early.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Noise-Space Design and Distribution Matching for One-Step Generators
PROPOSAL: Train generators that map a prior latent to full token sequences, comparing global and per-position priors under a distribution-matching objective that uses the frozen teacher's conditional probabilities on generator samples. Evaluate on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels, scoring quality, diversity and training speed against the teacher.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeating with seeds.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Per-position priors should raise diversity while quality stays near the teacher. The direction fails if all priors reach nearly the same scores.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Layer Pruning of the Teacher to Cut Sampling Cost
PROPOSAL: Remove transformer layers from the teacher autoregressive model by importance score and fine-tune the pruned network with distillation from the original. Measure per-token latency, model size and Frechet inception distance on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels, while the number of sampling steps stays equal to the number of tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare against the unpruned teacher and against a published structured-pruning method, repeating with seeds.
COST: 2000
PREDICTION: Latency should fall roughly in proportion to pruned layers with a small score change. The direction fails if quality drops quickly after the first few layers are removed.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Likelihood-Based Loss for a One-Step Generator Using Teacher Conditionals
PROPOSAL: Train a latent-to-sequence generator with a loss built from the frozen teacher's log-conditional probabilities of generated tokens, plus an entropy term that keeps the generator from collapsing onto a few sequences. Estimate gradients with a relaxed categorical sampler, and evaluate on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels using Frechet inception distance and recall.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeating with seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The entropy term should keep recall near the teacher and quality should approach the teacher's score. The direction fails if the generator collapses or the relaxed gradients prove too noisy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Correlation Heads for Larger Token Sets in Set Prediction
PROPOSAL: Extend a set-prediction sampler with a small head that models pairwise dependence between tokens inside each set, then enlarge the sets so that sampling takes fewer rounds. Evaluate on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels using Frechet inception distance and recall, tracking quality as the set size grows from a handful to many tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard set-prediction sampler and against the teacher sampled token by token, repeating with seeds.
COST: 200
PREDICTION: The correlation head should slow the loss of quality as sets grow. The direction fails if quality still drops quickly at large set sizes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training Speed of Distribution Matching Against Mapping-Based Distillation
PROPOSAL: Train a one-step generator with distribution matching and a mapping-based student from the same frozen teacher, recording image quality against wall-clock training time on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels. Plot Frechet inception distance as a function of elapsed time for each method, and note where each curve flattens.
CONTROLS: Compare against the teacher sampled token by token and against a published one-step distillation, repeating with seeds.
COST: 512
PREDICTION: Distribution matching should reach a given score sooner than the mapping-based student. The direction fails if both curves flatten at the same point and time.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Key-Value Memory Reduction for Token-by-Token Sampling
PROPOSAL: Compress the cache of keys and values that the teacher stores during sampling, using quantisation and eviction of tokens that attend weakly. Measure peak memory, per-token latency and Frechet inception distance on class-conditional ImageNet at 256 by 256 pixels, while sampling still proceeds one token after another.
CONTROLS: Compare against the full cache and against a published cache-compression method, repeating with seeds.
COST: 512
PREDICTION: Peak memory should fall by a large fraction with a small change in score. The direction fails if quality drops once the cache is compressed beyond a modest level.
